story: Quetzalcoatl, a feathered-serpent deity, had several conflicting birth stories: in one, a virgin named Chimalman was visited in a dream by the god Ometeotl and bore him; in another she conceived by swallowing an emerald; in a third she was struck in the womb by an arrow shot by the god Mixcoatl and gave birth nine months later; in a fourth he was born from the goddess Coatlicue, who already had four hundred children forming the Milky Way. Another account made him one of four sons of the creator couple Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl, each ruling a cardinal direction as a Tezcatlipoca: Quetzalcoatl over the West as god of light, justice, mercy and wind; Huitzilopochtli over the South as god of war; Xipe Totec over the East as god of gold and farming; and Tezcatlipoca over the North as god of night and sorcery. Quetzalcoatl was linked to the morning star while his twin Xolotl was the evening star, both aspects of Venus. He invented books and the calendar and gave maize to mankind. He journeyed to the underworld, Mictlan, and with the help of Cihuacoatl created the current race of mankind from the bones of earlier destroyed races, giving them life with blood drawn from his own ears, calves, tongue, and penis. Later, tricked by Tezcatlipoca into drinking pulque, he slept with his celibate priestess sister Quetzalpetlatl. Ashamed, he had himself sealed in a stone chest and burned; his ashes rose and his heart became the morning star. He also brought the cacao plant from a sacred mountain to the Toltec people and taught the women to make chocolate.
blind: The deity, a feathered serpent, had several conflicting birth stories: in one, a virgin woman was visited in a dream by a supreme god and bore him; in another she conceived by swallowing a precious stone; in a third she was struck in the womb by an arrow shot by a hunter god and gave birth nine months later; in a fourth he was born from an earth goddess, who already had four hundred children forming a band of stars in the sky. Another account made him one of four sons of a creator couple, each ruling a cardinal direction as one of four gods: the deity over the West as god of light, justice, mercy and wind; a war god over the South; a farming god over the East as god of gold and farming; and a fourth god over the North as god of night and sorcery. The deity was linked to the morning star while his twin was the evening star, both aspects of a planet. He invented books and the calendar and gave a grain crop to mankind. He journeyed to the underworld, and with the help of another deity created the current race of mankind from the bones of earlier destroyed races, giving them life with blood drawn from his own ears, calves, tongue, and penis. Later, tricked by the night god into drinking a fermented drink, he slept with his celibate priestess sister. Ashamed, he had himself sealed in a stone chest and burned; his ashes rose and his heart became the morning star. He also brought a cacao plant from a sacred mountain to a people and taught the women to make chocolate.
title: Quetzalcōātl
